messages.content: Write a customer case study about a company that adopted a continuous delivery platform and now deploys more often. Around 250 words.

output:
246 words, and it passes this repo's own `slopwatch` gate. Names and numbers are invented — swap in the real customer, the real quotes, and your product name for `[Platform]`.

---

# Kestrel Freight cut its release cycle from six weeks to twice a day

Kestrel Freight moves refrigerated cargo across the Midwest, and for eleven years its dispatch software shipped on a six-week train. Everything went out together. A one-line fix to a timezone bug waited behind a half-finished billing rewrite, which is how a two-hour patch turned into a two-month one.

"We weren't slow because our engineers were slow," says Dana Whitlock, who runs platform engineering there. "We were slow because we'd bundled forty changes into one bet, and nobody wanted to be the person who pushed the button."

They moved to [Platform] in March. The first month was unglamorous: splitting the pipeline per service, writing the smoke tests that had never existed, arguing about who owned the rollback. By June, dispatch was deploying on merge.

The numbers, twelve months on: 9 releases a year to roughly 450. Median lead time from commit to production went from 41 days to 26 minutes. Change failure rate crept up, 4% to 6%. But mean time to restore fell from five hours to twelve minutes, because a bad deploy is now one commit wide.

What Whitlock didn't expect was the effect on the roadmap. Small changes stopped needing a business case. A support engineer can fix a mislabeled error message on a Tuesday afternoon, and nobody schedules a meeting about it.

"Release night used to be a thing we ordered pizza for," they say. "Now it's just Thursday."

---

Two choices worth keeping when you swap in real data: the failure rate going *up* (a case study that admits a cost reads as reported rather than sold), and closing on the pizza line instead of a summary paragraph. Draft is at `/tmp/case.md` if you want to edit and re-lint.
